paper.title: ArcMemo: Abstract Reasoning Composition with Lifelong LLM Memory
paper.central_claim: Concept-level (abstract, modular, natural-language) memory distilled from solution traces and selectively retrieved into the prompt enables test-time continual learning without weight updates; on ARC-AGI-1 it gives a 7.5% relative gain over a strong no-memory baseline (55.17 to 59.33), is the only memory design above baseline at all tested inference scales, and dynamically updating memory at test time outperforms fixed settings.

signatures.object: Flat external memory of concept entries (OE: situation/suggestion pairs; PS: parameterized typed types/structures/routines with relevance cues and implementation notes) injected into an o4-mini program-synthesis solver prompt; baselines: no memory, frozen Dynamic-Cheatsheet-style summary.
signatures.information: Verified solution traces (post-hoc derivation / pseudocode) of seed puzzles and, in the continual variant, self-generated solutions; a correctness feedback signal is assumed available; labels may be absent at inference; evaluation puzzles are separate from the 160 train-split seeds.
signatures.operation: Write: GPT-4.1 abstracts a solution into OE or PS entries (PS revises existing entries using a compressed view of memory). Read: OE = VLM caption of the puzzle + LLM top-k match against situation fields; PS = reasoning-model exploration guided by relevance cues and type annotations.
signatures.output: Subset of concept entries injected into the solver prompt.
signatures.conditions: Trace-level correctness feedback required; abstract entries break embedding retrieval, hence reasoning-based selection.
signatures.feedback: Execution of the synthesized program against reference pairs (retries) and test cases.
signatures.selection_rule: No measured admission or marginal-utility test; entries come from (assumed) verified-correct solutions; read-time top-k / reasoning-based selection only.
signatures.persistence: Additive flat store; OE write ignores existing contents; PS can revise; no deletion, forgetting, versioning, rollback or conflict handling (deferred to future work).
signatures.later_use: Retrieved for each new puzzle in later passes.
signatures.claimed_effect: Official score 55.17 -> 59.33 at 0 retries (ARC-AGI-1, 100 validation puzzles, o4-mini, mean of 3 runs); only memory design above baseline in all 9 inference-scale cells.
signatures.failure_boundary: Needs feedback; retrieval-specificity tension; flat store; single benchmark; gains concentrate at low inference compute.

retention_trace.proposed_change: new/revised concept entries abstracted from verified solution traces
retention_trace.selection_data_rule: assumed-correct traces only; no marginal-effect test
retention_trace.measured_gain: +4.16 official points at retry0, +0.17..+2.5 at other scales (within ~1 baseline SD)

signatures.object: OE concept memory updated during evaluation (every 10 problems) with newly self-generated solutions.
signatures.information: Solver outputs on the evaluation stream; which feedback certifies a solution before it is written (reference pairs vs hidden test outputs) is not stated.
signatures.operation: Re-run the OE write operation on new solutions every k=10 problems, then read as in S1.
signatures.output: Grown OE memory used by later problems/passes.
signatures.conditions: Order and batching dependence acknowledged; fixed memory used elsewhere to avoid confounding.
signatures.feedback: Self-generated solutions verified by tests (source unspecified).
signatures.later_use: Subsequent problems and subsequent retry passes over the test set.
signatures.claimed_effect: Improvement emerges at higher retry depth (OE only).
signatures.failure_boundary: Evaluation stream equals update stream; PS not tested; mixed cells (better than fixed in 4/9).

gap.author_gap: Reasoning insights are discarded when the context resets; existing reasoning memories are instance-level (coupled to the source problem) or monolithic summaries, which transfer poorly and scale badly without selection.
gap.checked_gap: Partly confirmed. The changed object (entry abstraction level + read-time selection) is specific and neighbours are named, but no experiment shows instance-level memories failing on ARC while abstract ones succeed, and the authors own n=10 pilot finds more specific concepts solve more.

lineage.closest_adjacent: Dynamic Cheatsheet (compared as frozen baseline), Buffer of Thoughts, Think-in-Memory, concurrent MemP (abstraction of action sequences in agentic settings)
lineage.source_version: as described in 2509.04439v3 related-work text; neighbour papers are not in the pinned materials

gap.residue: Retrieval over abstract entries is hard (embedding retrieval hurt); consolidation/hierarchy and order-robust updates left to future work.
gap.stakes: Without abstraction and selection a growing reasoning memory either overflows context or distracts the solver.
gap.method_response: Concept formats (OE/PS) written by abstraction prompts, reasoning-based selection, optional continual updates.
gap.remaining_gap: No consolidation or admission gate, no instance-level control, one benchmark, update-order sensitivity.
unresolved: Full texts of Dynamic Cheatsheet, Buffer of Thoughts and MemP are not pinned, so the neighbour comparison relies on this paper description (request listed in batch report).

claims.text: ArcMemo-PS improves the official ARC-AGI-1 score over a no-memory o4-mini baseline (59.33 vs 55.17) and is above baseline at all tested inference scales.
claims.setting: o4-mini (medium), 100 random public-validation puzzles, program-synthesis evaluation with execution feedback, fixed memory seeded from 160 hand-written train-split solutions
claims.baseline_control: same model, same retries and parallel attempts, no memory; plus frozen cheatsheet and OE variants
claims.selection_vs_test: seeds from train split, evaluation on validation split (separate)
claims.result_denominator: 100 puzzles x 3 runs; official oracle@2 59.33 (SD 0.29) vs 55.17 (SD 3.18); retry1 67.33 vs 66.67; retry2 70.83 vs 69.00
claims.allowed_conclusion: A small positive effect (about 1.3 baseline SD at retry0, below 1 SD elsewhere) on a 100-puzzle subset; not shown to be independent of extra exploration.

claims.text: Reasoning-based concept selection improves performance and token cost.
claims.setting: PS with vs without selection, same seeds
claims.result_denominator: better with selection in 7/9 cells; retry0 k=2 59.33 vs 55.17; reversed at retry1/2 k=3
claims.allowed_conclusion: Selection supplies the whole gain at the official standard-compute setting and little at higher retry depth.

claims.text: Dynamically updating memory at test time outperforms fixed memory (self-improvement).
claims.setting: OE only, update every 10 problems with self-generated solutions
claims.selection_vs_test: update stream equals evaluation stream; order dependent
claims.result_denominator: continual better in 4/9 cells (retry2 all three, retry1 k1), worse in 4/9, equal in 1
claims.allowed_conclusion: At most a retry-depth-dependent gain for OE, not established for PS; abstract claim of outperforming fixed settings is overstated.

claims.text: Abstract, modular concepts are the most consistent memory design (vs instance-level or summary memory).
claims.setting: PS and OE vs frozen cheatsheet vs no memory
claims.result_denominator: PS above baseline in 9/9 cells, cheatsheet 6/9, OE 3/9
claims.allowed_conclusion: PS is the only variant above no-memory everywhere; the abstraction-vs-instance claim itself is untested.

claims.text: New solves under ArcMemo are more attributable to memory content (100%) than under the cheatsheet (40%).
claims.setting: manual inspection of 10 puzzles that differ between two systems
claims.allowed_conclusion: Suggestive only; authors themselves caveat causal reading.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Both seats 'retained', re-checked: the fixed concept store (abstracted from train-split seed solutions) is read on separate validation puzzles and PS beats the same-budget store-off baseline in all 9 Table 4 cells. The gain is small (≈1 SD) and the self-generated continual-update claim is only retry-2/OE (opus:O03) — retained, not improver.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: An LLM-abstracted, selectively retrieved concept memory seeded from 160 external solutions gives a small, noisy gain (about +4 points official score at 0 retries, at most +2.5 at higher scales, about one baseline SD or less) on a 100-puzzle ARC-AGI-1 validation subset with o4-mini; the gain at standard compute depends on the selection step; self-generated continual updates help only at the highest retry depth for the OE format and PS is not tested.
assessment.not_supported: That abstraction beats instance-level memory; that test-time updating outperforms fixed memory in general; that gains are independent of extra exploration tokens.
unresolved: Which feedback certifies traces written during continual updates
Whether the cheatsheet baseline is seeded identically
Overlap between the n=10 validation design pilots and the 100-puzzle evaluation subset (opus:O05).

E.measurement.reason: Opus sides with sol. The verifier is exact execution of the generated program on each puzzle's test cases (opus:O01) under the official oracle@2 metric, and a strict single-program-solves-all regime (Table 5) reproduces the ordering; for this central claim the metric and verifier cannot be satisfied by non-target factors. son55's docking reason (public-ARC exposure) is, by its own note, scored under E.holdout; A2 keeps it there.
